title: a carpenter's son from a nowhere town, not a stained-glass window
hookLine: a carpenter's son from a nowhere town, not a stained-glass window
carry: he ate with the wrong people on purpose
tomorrow: the prayer a room says without a page

cards: A stained-glass window, lit from behind. A painting with a golden circle around his head. A calm face on a card in a hospital waiting room.
Those are the usual pictures of Jesus. Now try a different one. A man with rough hands, dust from his trade on his clothes.
A family the neighbors knew by name. When he started to teach, the neighbors weren't impressed. They were confused.

teach.b: Start with the name. Jesus is the English form of a Greek name, which comes from the Hebrew Yeshua, the same name as Joshua. It means, roughly, God saves.

It wasn't a rare name; one of Paul's letters mentions another man called Jesus. Then the job. When he comes home to teach, the neighbors ask, in the old English: "Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary?"
The Greek word is tekton: a builder, a craftsman. It could mean wood, and it could mean stone. Either way, a working man with a trade.
Then the town. Nazareth, in Galilee, a place nobody in the story expects much from.

When one man first hears where Jesus is from, he says: "Can there any good thing come out of Nazareth?" His friend answers: "Come and see." But in Mark's Gospel, what gets people talking isn't where he came from.

teach.h: A TABLE WITH THE WRONG PEOPLE.
teach.b: He sits down at the house of a tax collector, at a table full of people others avoided. Some religious teachers ask his followers how he can eat with tax collectors and sinners.
He answers: healthy people don't need a doctor. Sick people do. The meal itself is the message.
Christians say much more about Jesus: that he is the Son of God, that he died and rose again. The path gets to all of that.

how: Christians come to know Jesus mainly through the four Gospels, read aloud in church services, and they pray to him or in his name.

games.q: you're a teacher in Galilee. a tax collector, a man people resent, invites you to dinner with his friends. what do you do?
o: decline politely, to keep your good name.
go, and sit down at the table.
send a message to him instead.
games.why: Jesus went. when asked why, he said healthy people don't need a doctor; sick people do. the table was the point.

practice: Here's the practice. Sit, and picture a table you've eaten at. Notice who usually sits there.

Now picture one person who usually doesn't: someone you'd never think to invite. Give them a chair, just in your mind, and stay with the fuller table for a while. If you pray, you can bring them into it.

wordCard.voice: Jesus. Yeshua: God saves. A builder's name from a small town, at the center of the whole Christian path. Tenth word.

orig.note: Hebrew and Aramaic. the same name as Joshua. Greek wrote it Iēsous, and English got Jesus.

carryVoice: Your line: he ate with the wrong people on purpose. In the Gospels, that's what got him talked about. Day ten.
